summary: Stuart H. Blackburn is an Indologist who studied at Wesleyan University (~1962–1966) and the University of California, Berkeley (~1973–1980). He held a post at SOAS University of London from circa 1993 to 2011.

Stuart Henry Buck (1911–1997) was a scholar in Tibetology who earned an A.B. from Harvard University (~1929–1933). He served as an intelligence analyst at the National Security Agency from circa 1947 to 1980.

Stuart Piggott (1910–1996) worked in archaeology and Indology, studying at Churcher's College, UCL, and the UCL Institute of Archaeology. He held posts at Reading Museum, as Professor of Archaeology at the University of Edinburgh, and at Oxford.
Stuart Ray Sarbacker is a scholar in religious studies, Indology, and philosophy. He completed his Ph.D. at the University of Wisconsin-Madison in 2001 under the supervision of David M. Knipe.

Su Bai (1922–2018) worked in archaeology, Buddhist studies, and Sinology. He completed graduate studies at Peking University (1940–1944) under Chengjun Feng, Zuoyun Sun, Rong Geng, and Yongtong Tang, and served as a professor there from 1948 to 2004.

Subhadradis Diskul (1923–2003) studied at Chulalongkorn, École du Louvre under Philippe Stern, and the University of London. He was curator at Bangkok's National Museum, professor and rector at Silpakorn University, and president of the Siam Society.

Subhash Chandra works in computational linguistics and Indology. He completed his Ph.D. at Jawaharlal Nehru University (2007–2012) and serves as a professor at the University of Delhi (attested 2026).

Subhash Kak is an Indologist who studied at NIT Srinagar and IIT Delhi under P. V. Indiresan. He held posts at Louisiana State University (1979) and served as Regents Professor at Oklahoma State University (2007).

Subodhkant Mishra, working in Indology and religious studies, studied at Banaras Hindu University, University of Delhi, and IGNOU. He held posts at Shree Mahendra Das Degree College, Indus University, and became Assistant Professor at Central University of Punjab in 2026.

Subrata K. Mitra studied at Utkal University, Delhi, JNU, and Rochester (Ph.D.). He served as Head of Political Science at Heidelberg University (1994–2014) and Director and Research Professor at the National University of Singapore (2015–2018).
Sucharita Adluri is an Indologist and religious studies scholar who earned a Ph.D. from the University of Pennsylvania. In 2009, she became a professor at Cleveland State University.

Sucheng Chan is a historian who studied at Swarthmore College, the University of Hawaiʻi at Mānoa, and the University of California, Berkeley. She is an emerita professor at the University of California, Santa Barbara (~2006).
Sudan Shakya is a scholar in Buddhist studies and Indology who holds a post as professor at Shuchiin University (attested 2013–2017, 2026).

Sudarshan Chakradhari is an archaeology and Indology scholar who completed a Ph.D. at Banaras Hindu University (2013–2019). In 2023, he was appointed Assistant Professor at Babasaheb Bhimrao Ambedkar University.

Sudhir Kakar (1938–2024), an Indologist and religious studies scholar, studied at Gujarat, Mannheim, Vienna, and Sigmund-Freud-Institut. He taught at Harvard, IIM Ahmedabad, and IIT Delhi, and was a visiting professor at institutions including INSEAD and Chicago.

Sudhākara Dvivedī (1855–1910) was an Indologist who studied under Devakṛṣṇa. He served as librarian and later professor and head of mathematics at Sampurnanand Sanskrit University, and taught mathematics and astrology at Sanskrit College and University.

Sue Hamilton is a scholar of Buddhist studies, Indology, and philosophy. She earned a D.Phil. at Oxford under Alexis Sanderson and Richard Gombrich, and later served as Director and Professor of Prehistory at University College London (2014–2022).
Suehiro Tanemura (1933–2004) studied at the University of Tokyo (~1953–1957). He held academic posts at Tokyo Metropolitan University (~1968–1986) and Kokugakuin University (~1986–1998).
Sujeet Kumar works in computational fields and Indology. He has held academic posts at the Indian Institute of Technology Kharagpur and B.P. Mandal College of Engineering.

Suk Fun Ng is a scholar in Buddhist studies and Sinology who earned a Ph.D. at the University of Hong Kong under Jing Yin, Yakupitiyage Karunadasa, and K. L. Dhammajoti. She serves as a professor at Hong Kong Baptist University.
